Gene Description

AGTRAP (ATRAP) is a small, ubiquitously expressed integral membrane protein of 159 amino acids with three transmembrane helices, an extracellular/lumenal N-terminus and a roughly 50-residue cytoplasmic C-terminal tail. It sits in endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and endocytic vesicle membranes and at the plasma membrane, and its vesicles move constitutively toward the cell surface. Its defining activity is binding the carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic tail of the type-1 angiotensin II receptor (AGTR1) through its own C-terminal tail; the interaction is selective for AT1 and does not extend to the AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin B2, endothelin B or beta2-adrenergic receptors. Through it AGTRAP restrains angiotensin II signalling: it promotes AT1 receptor internalization and lowers receptor density at the cell surface, and cells over-expressing it show reduced phospholipase C activation, inositol lipid generation, c-fos induction and proliferation in response to angiotensin II. Mice lacking Atrap have elevated arterial blood pressure, expanded plasma volume and increased surface AT1 receptor in the renal cortex, where the protein is most abundant in the proximal tubule brush border; human AGTRAP mRNA is highest in kidney, heart, pancreas and thyroid. In heart, AGTRAP additionally binds the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2a and stimulates its calcium uptake, accelerating cytosolic calcium decay and ventricular relaxation - an activity independent of the angiotensin receptor. Further reported partners include the scaffold RACK1, the phosphatidylinositol transfer protein PITPNC1/RdgB-beta, which AGTRAP recruits to membranes, and FAM114A1. AGTRAP is itself neither a receptor nor an enzyme: it has no G-protein coupling and no catalytic activity.

GO_REF:0000044 		ACCEPT
Summary: Correct. UniProt's Golgi apparatus membrane SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line for AGTRAP carries ECO:0000269|PubMed:12960423, so this keyword-derived row traces to a direct microscopy result on the protein rather than to a prediction.
Reason: PubMed:12960423 localised ATRAP by immunofluorescence and electron microscopy to perinuclear vesicular membranes corresponding to endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and endocytic vesicles, and this is the experimental basis of the three UniProt SubCell terms. The protein is a multi-pass membrane protein (three predicted TM helices, UniProt FT 24-44, 56-76, 87-107), so a membrane-qualified location is the right granularity.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:12960423
colocalization analysis by immunofluorescence shows that ATRAP colocalizes in an intracellular vesicular compartment corresponding to endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, and endocytic vesicles
GO:0001666 response to hypoxia
IEA
GO_REF:0000107 		MARK AS OVER ANNOTATED
Summary: Over-annotated. The whole annotation rests on a single rat IEP - a transcript abundance change in a neonatal-brain hypoxic-preconditioning experiment - projected into human by orthology.
Reason: The donor was resolved and then its own evidence queried rather than assumed: UniProtKB:Q642A2 is rat Agtrap (ATRAP_RAT, Swiss-Prot, 160 aa, a true orthologue), and its only experimental support for GO:0001666 is one IEP from PubMed:17033689, 'Vascular response to hypoxic preconditioning in the immature brain'. Querying QuickGO by that reference returns two annotations in all of GOA - rat Agtrap and rat Angptl4 - both IEP, i.e. the paper's GO footprint is an expression-pattern readout and nothing more. An expression change formally satisfies 'response to' in the source species, but projecting a tissue- and development-stage-specific response term across species asserts something about human AGTRAP that has never been tested. Kept rather than removed because the rat observation itself is not in doubt.

GO:0004945 angiotensin type II receptor activity
IEA
GO_REF:0000107 		REMOVE
Summary: Wrong, and demonstrably so in two independent ways. AGTRAP is not a receptor, and the gene's founding paper specifically tested and excluded any AT2 interaction; the annotation traces to an MGI row taken from a paper about Agtr2, not Agtrap.
Reason: Biology first, because the argument does not depend on provenance. GO:0004945 is defined as 'An angiotensin receptor activity that acts via Gi protein coupling and cGMP (NO) generation', and the qualifier here is enables - i.e. the assertion is that AGTRAP is a functional AT2 receptor. AGTRAP is a 159-residue protein with three transmembrane helices (UniProt FT 24-44, 56-76, 87-107), not a seven-pass GPCR, and nothing in its record involves G-protein coupling. PubMed:10358057 assayed exactly this question and reported that ATRAP binds the AT1a C-terminal tail and specifically not AT2, so the term is contradicted by direct experiment on this protein, and it names the wrong receptor subtype for a protein whose own name is 'type-1'. Provenance second, and it explains how the row arose. The Compara donor UniProtKB:Q9WVK0 is mouse Agtrap, a true orthologue, but its GO:0004945 is an MGI IMP citing PubMed:10425188 - 'Increased vasoconstrictor response of the mouse lacking angiotensin II type 2 receptor', an Agtr2-knockout study whose abstract does not mention Agtrap. Querying QuickGO by reference rather than by gene shows that paper annotating three entities: Agt, Agtr2 (which correctly receives GO:0004945 enables by IGI) and Agtrap - two alphabetically adjacent symbols, one of which is an angiotensin receptor. The error is now in three species: rat Agtrap (Q642A2) carries GO:0004945 both by Ensembl IEA and by RGD ISO. Correcting the MGI row would clear all of them.

Summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted, and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
Reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q96AL5, an unreviewed 367-aa TrEMBL entry, not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein. Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of the screen set has.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:35414770
we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

PMID:16189514
Towards a proteome-scale map of the human protein-protein in... 		MODIFY
Summary: PITPNC1 (RdgB-beta) is one of only three AGTRAP two-hybrid partners with orthogonal support, and the only one that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself: a targeted study shows AGTRAP recruits the PITP domain of RdgB-beta to membranes, i.e. AGTRAP is the membrane anchor.
Reason: The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP, which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - 'brings together a protein ... with a membrane ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein' - which integral membrane tethers such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495's differentia describes the adaptor as reaching the membrane 'either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein', and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO's usage is broader than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956, PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels, is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it was measured, rather than promoted.
Proposed replacements: protein-membrane adaptor activity
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:21728994
interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment

Next-generation sequencing to generate interactome datasets. 		MARK AS OVER ANNOTATED
Summary: PDHX (O00330) appears only as a yeast two-hybrid hit, in 3 CCSB interactome releases (PMID:21516116, PMID:25416956, PMID:31515488) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal experiment supports it and protein binding conveys no molecular function, so the row is marked over-annotated rather than treated as evidence about AGTRAP.
Reason: All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617 evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 = 92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same way, so UniProt's NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20 of them disordered. PDHX is confined to the mitochondrial matrix, which that 52-residue cytosolic surface cannot reach in an intact cell. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP's 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record or in UniProt's curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn across this gene's binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).

Both partners are over-expressed as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20 of them disordered. FARS2 is confined to the mitochondrial matrix, which that 52-residue cytosolic surface cannot reach in an intact cell. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP's 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record or in UniProt's curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn across this gene's binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP's 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record or in UniProt's curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn across this gene's binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).

Summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted, and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
Reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q5JS98, an unreviewed 455-aa TrEMBL entry, not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein. Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of the screen set has.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:35414770
we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

Summary: FAM114A1 is a two-hybrid hit that a later targeted study took up and confirmed in native tissue, placing the AGTRAP-FAM114A1 pair upstream of AT1R abundance in cardiac fibroblasts. Kept, but protein binding is not a core function.
Reason: PMID:35671117 is titled for FAM114A1, not for AGTRAP, and states outright that it began from the published two-hybrid candidates and then validated this one by immunoprecipitation and Western blotting in mouse heart lysates and primary cardiac fibroblasts - i.e. an orthogonal assay at endogenous levels, which none of the other screen partners has. Loss of Fam114a1 raised AGTRAP protein and lowered AT1R, and siRNA knockdown of Agtrap reversed the Fam114a1-null phenotype, so the interaction is functional as well as physical. Retained as non-core because GO:0005515 itself conveys no molecular function and the regulatory direction runs from FAM114A1 onto AGTRAP rather than the reverse.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:35671117
we validated the interaction between AGTRAP and FAM114A1 in mouse heart lysates and cultured PMCFs by IP and Western blotting

Summary: PITPNC1 (RdgB-beta) is one of only three AGTRAP two-hybrid partners with orthogonal support, and the only one that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself: a targeted study shows AGTRAP recruits the PITP domain of RdgB-beta to membranes, i.e. AGTRAP is the membrane anchor.
Reason: The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP, which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - 'brings together a protein ... with a membrane ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein' - which integral membrane tethers such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495's differentia describes the adaptor as reaching the membrane 'either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein', and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO's usage is broader than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956, PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels, is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it was measured, rather than promoted.
Proposed replacements: protein-membrane adaptor activity
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:21728994
interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment

Summary: PCTP (Q9UKL6) appears only as a yeast two-hybrid hit, in 1 CCSB interactome release (PMID:25416956) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal experiment supports it and protein binding conveys no molecular function, so the row is marked over-annotated rather than treated as evidence about AGTRAP.
Reason: All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617 evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 = 92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same way, so UniProt's NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20 of them disordered. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP's 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record or in UniProt's curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn across this gene's binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).

Summary: SUCLA2 (Q9P2R7) appears only as a yeast two-hybrid hit, in 2 CCSB interactome releases (PMID:26871637, PMID:32296183) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal experiment supports it and protein binding conveys no molecular function, so the row is marked over-annotated rather than treated as evidence about AGTRAP.
Reason: All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617 evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 = 92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same way, so UniProt's NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20 of them disordered. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP's 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record or in UniProt's curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn across this gene's binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).

GO:0005515 protein binding
IPI
Q6RW13-2
PMID:32296183
A reference map of the human binary protein interactome. 		KEEP AS NON CORE
Summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted, and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
Reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q96AL5, an unreviewed 367-aa TrEMBL entry, not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein. Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of the screen set has.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:35414770
we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

Q6RW13-2
PMID:32296183
A reference map of the human binary protein interactome. 		MODIFY
Summary: PITPNC1 (RdgB-beta) is one of only three AGTRAP two-hybrid partners with orthogonal support, and the only one that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself: a targeted study shows AGTRAP recruits the PITP domain of RdgB-beta to membranes, i.e. AGTRAP is the membrane anchor.
Reason: The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP, which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - 'brings together a protein ... with a membrane ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein' - which integral membrane tethers such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495's differentia describes the adaptor as reaching the membrane 'either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein', and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO's usage is broader than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956, PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels, is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it was measured, rather than promoted.
Proposed replacements: protein-membrane adaptor activity
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:21728994
interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment

Summary: The sign is wrong. This is an InterPro family-name mapping asserting that AGTRAP is part of the angiotensin-activated pathway, whereas every measurement on the protein shows it damping that pathway.

GO:0031702 type 1 angiotensin receptor binding
IPI
PMID:12960423
The angiotensin II type I receptor-associated protein, ATRAP... 		NEW
Summary: Proposed. This is the interaction the gene is named for, it is measured, UniProt curates it on the human entry and gives it a sequence feature, and the mouse orthologue carries it in GO - yet human GOA has no trace of it.
Reason: AGTRAP was isolated as a binder of the AT1a receptor's carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic domain, and the binding is subtype-selective: PubMed:10358057 tested AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin B2, endothelin B and beta2-adrenergic tails and found none of them bound. PubMed:12960423 mapped the requirement to AGTRAP's own C-terminal tail by deletion, and UniProt records the interaction on the human entry (SUBUNIT with ECO:0000269) plus a REGION 110..122 feature annotated 'Interaction with AGTR1'. The mouse orthologue already carries this as GO:0005515 IPI with P29754 (Agtr1a) from PubMed:10358057; the human gene carries 187 protein binding rows, none of them AGTR1. GO:0031702 is chosen over its parent GO:0031701 because the measured fact is precisely the subtype selectivity. The term is already established for proteins that bind the receptor's cytoplasmic face rather than its ligand pocket, so this is not a novel use of it: of its 197 annotations over 188 gene products, 16 entities hold it by non-IEA evidence, and those include ARRB2, JAK2, TYK2 and ARAP1, each by rat IPI, alongside AGT (the ligand precursor; human IPI, mouse IDA). What is thin is human coverage - five human entities, of which only AGT and BDKRB2 are IPI and the other three are Ensembl projections - and none of them is an accessory protein of AGTRAP's kind. Evidence code, stated with its difficulty rather than asserted. IPI on PubMed:12960423 rests on two things. First, UniProt tags that paper with ECO:0000269 on the human entry for FUNCTION, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION - a curator judgement made with the full text, which this review does not have (PMC284805 returns no extractable body). Second, NLM indexes PubMed:12960423 with the MeSH organism term 'Humans' and with neither 'Animals' nor 'Mice', whereas the founding mouse paper PubMed:10358057 is indexed 'Animals' + 'Mice' and not 'Humans'. The indexing discriminates the two papers, and the absence of 'Animals' is hard to account for if the experiments had used mouse material. Against that sits a real discrepancy that should not be buried: the abstract numbers the protein's hydrophobic domains 14-36, 55-77 and 88-108 with a cytoplasmic tail at 109-161, and 161 aa is mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0), not human Q6RW13 (159 aa, TOPO_DOM 108..159). The likeliest reconciliation is that the authors kept the residue numbering of the sequence first published in PubMed:10358057 while working with human constructs, but that cannot be confirmed without the full text. IPI is therefore retained on explicit deference to the UniProt curator, with the numbering conflict recorded; if the full text shows rodent constructs, the correct code is ISS with UniProtKB:Q9WVK0 and the supporting entity becomes the murine AT1a receptor UniProtKB:P29754 rather than human AGTR1 UniProtKB:P30556 - the code and the partner accession change together, and the term does not change either way. The founding characterisation (PubMed:10358057) used the mouse protein and mouse AT1a and is cited as corroboration rather than as the human evidence.

ATRAP interacts specifically with the carboxyl-terminal domain of the AT1a receptor but not with those of angiotensin II type 2 (AT2), m3 muscarinic acetylcholine, bradykinin B2, endothelin B, and beta2-adrenergic receptors.

Summary: Proposed. A second, AT1-receptor-independent molecular activity: AGTRAP binds the cardiac calcium pump SERCA2a and increases its calcium uptake. Absent from GO in every form.
Reason: PubMed:27015675 is titled for SERCA2a rather than for AGTRAP, which is why an AGTRAP-keyed search does not surface it. It identifies SERCA2a in Atrap pull-downs by MALDI-MS, confirms the interaction by co-immunoprecipitation and by surface plasmon resonance, and shows Atrap increases SERCA-dependent calcium uptake in isolated sarcoplasmic reticulum vesicles; Atrap-null myocytes have prolonged calcium-transient decay and sarcomere re-lengthening, and the mice a markedly reduced maximum ventricular filling rate with unchanged ejection fraction. GO:0141109 'binds to and increases the activity of a transporter' is the sibling of GO:0141110, which phospholamban holds by IDA for the inhibitory version of the same regulation, so the ontology already models this relationship. The knockout physiology is unambiguously mouse, hence ISS with mouse Agtrap as the supporting entity rather than IDA. One caveat in the other direction, recorded so it can be revisited: NLM indexes PubMed:27015675 with 'Humans' as well as 'Animals', and with 'HEK293 Cells', so the binding measurements may have used human constructs even though the calcium-uptake and knockout work did not. ISS is the conservative reading; confirming human constructs would license IPI for the interaction half. Stated as one well-controlled study, not as settled biology.
Supporting Evidence:
PMID:27015675
Sequencing by MALDI-MS of the isolated complexes showed that Atrap interacts with the cardiac Ca(2+)-ATPase SERCA2a.
PMID:27015675
Atrap enhanced the SERCA-dependent Ca(2+) uptake in isolated SR membrane vesicles.

Core Functions

Selective binding partner and negative regulator of the type-1 angiotensin II receptor. AGTRAP's cytoplasmic C-terminal tail, and specifically the region around residues 110-122, engages the AT1 receptor's own carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic tail; the interaction does not extend to AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin B2, endothelin B or beta2-adrenergic receptors. AGTRAP cycles on endoplasmic-reticulum-, Golgi- and endosome-derived vesicles that translocate constitutively toward the plasma membrane, and the effect of the interaction is to accelerate AT1 receptor internalization and lower its surface density, so that angiotensin II produces less phospholipase C activation, less inositol lipid generation, less c-fos induction and less proliferation. Losing the protein in mouse raises surface AT1 receptor in the renal cortex and raises arterial blood pressure.

type 1 angiotensin receptor binding

    - **partners:** AGTR1, RACK1, PITPNC1, ATP2A2, USP14, PBX3, PSMB8, PSMB10

Stimulator of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2a in cardiac muscle, independent of any angiotensin receptor. AGTRAP binds SERCA2a directly and raises its calcium uptake rate, speeding cytosolic calcium decay and sarcomere re-lengthening; losing the protein slows ventricular filling without changing contractile amplitude or ejection fraction. This is the mirror image of phospholamban, which binds the same pump and inhibits it. Recorded because it is a directly measured activity rather than an inference from the gene's name, but it rests on a single study carried out entirely in mouse.

Molecular Function:
transporter activator activity
Supporting Evidence:
  • PMID:27015675
    Atrap enhanced the SERCA-dependent Ca(2+) uptake in isolated SR membrane vesicles.
  • PMID:27015675
    The interaction between Atrap and SERCA2a was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation and by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy.

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: MGI annotation request: mouse Agtrap (MGI:1339977) carries GO:0004945 angiotensin type II receptor activity (enables, IMP) and GO:0008217 (IMP) from PMID:10425188, which is an Agtr2-knockout study that assays no Agtrap allele; Agtr2 correctly receives GO:0004945 from the same paper. Retiring the GO:0004945 row would also clear the Ensembl projections onto human AGTRAP and rat Agtrap and the ISO copy RGD makes from it - one edit fixing four annotations in three species. The GO:0008217 row should be re-referenced to PMID:20093357 rather than retired, since the Atrap-knockout blood pressure phenotype is real.

Suggested experts: Dzau VJ, Tamura K, Horiuchi M

Q: Why does human AGTRAP have 187 protein binding rows and not one of them AGTR1, when UniProt curates the interaction on the human entry with ECO:0000269, gives it a REGION 110..122 feature, and the mouse orthologue holds it as GO:0005515 IPI with P29754? The same applies to RACK1 (P63244), supported by four orthogonal assays in PMID:11733189. Checking from the partners' side rather than AGTRAP's shows the gap is symmetric, so it is not a property of this gene's record: PMID:12960423, PMID:11733189, PMID:21728994, PMID:27015675 and PMID:35414770 have produced zero GO annotations on human AGTR1, RACK1, PITPNC1, ATP2A2 and canonical PBX3 respectively. The one counter-example shows it is fixable - MGI curated PMID:35671117 reciprocally on both mouse partners (Fam114a1 IPI with Q9WVK0, Agtrap IPI with Q9D281), while neither human partner received anything.

Suggested experts: Cockcroft S, Orchard S

Q: GO:0031702 type 1 angiotensin receptor binding carries 197 annotations over 188 gene products, but only 16 entities hold it by non-IEA evidence and the experimental weight sits almost entirely in rat: ARRB2, JAK2, TYK2 and ARAP1 each by IPI. Only five human entities hold the term at all, and only AGT and BDKRB2 by IPI. Should those rat IPIs be projected to their human orthologues, and is the AT1 receptor's cytoplasmic interactome being under-annotated in human as a result?

Q: GOA imported all 188 of AGTRAP's binding rows from two-hybrid screens and none from the 23 IntAct pairs with AP-MS, co-IP or BioID support, which are almost all membrane proteins (CYB5D2, ENPP6, MBLAC2, TMEM47, TMEM106B, LAMP5, SLC15A3, SLC15A4, TMEM63A, CFTR, PAFAH2). Is that selection deliberate, and would the membrane set be a better basis for annotating a three-pass membrane protein?

Suggested experts: Orchard S, Vidal M

Q: Does human AGTRAP stimulate SERCA2a as the mouse protein does (PMID:27015675), and is the activity confined to SERCA2a or shared with SERCA1 and SERCA3? If it generalises, GO:1901896 positive regulation of ATPase-coupled calcium transmembrane transporter activity would belong on the gene alongside the molecular function proposed here.

Suggested experts: Castrop H, Kockskamper J

Q: Is the AGTRAP homodimer real? The only evidence is a single HuRI self-pair on isoform 2, which lacks residues 115-121 from within the AGTR1-interaction region - so if the protein does oligomerise, the tested species is the one least likely to be engaging the receptor.

Suggested experts: Luck K, Calderwood MA

Q: Both ISS rows proposed here (GO:0002092, GO:0141109) transfer from mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0), which holds neither term - so as written they are ISS from an ortholog with nothing to transfer. The underlying experiments are mouse, so the annotations belong on the mouse gene first: Agtrap GO:0141109 by IDA from PubMed:27015675 (pull-down, co-immunoprecipitation, surface plasmon resonance and a calcium-uptake increase), and Agtrap GO:0002092 by IMP from PubMed:11162453 and PubMed:15757644. Would MGI make those, so the human transfers have a source?

Suggested experts: Castrop H, Kockskamper J

Q: GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity is defined as bringing a protein to a membrane 'either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein', yet SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold it and are themselves integral membrane proteins that satisfy neither clause - as would AGTRAP, which anchors PITPNC1 by being the membrane protein. Should the differentia be widened to cover an integral membrane protein acting as the tether, rather than leaving each such annotation to be justified per gene?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Co-immunoprecipitate endogenous AGTRAP and AGTR1 from human kidney proximal tubule or cardiac tissue at native expression, and submit the result to IntAct. Every existing AGTRAP-AGTR1 experiment is an over-expression assay, several of them on the mouse protein, which is the likeliest reason the interaction never entered human GOA.

Hypothesis: AGTRAP and AGTR1 associate at endogenous expression in the tissues where both are abundant, and the interaction's absence from human GOA is a curation gap rather than a biological one.

Type: Endogenous co-immunoprecipitation from human tissue

Experiment: Map the AGTRAP side of the interface by scanning alanine substitutions across residues 108-140 in a surface-AT1R internalization assay, then test whether the isoform-2 deletion (residues 115-121) is loss-of-function. That would say whether the two main isoforms differ in receptor regulation and would replace UniProt's unevidenced REGION 110..122 with mapped contacts.

Hypothesis: The AGTR1-binding determinant lies within AGTRAP residues 108-140, and isoform 2, which deletes residues 115-121 from that region, is impaired for receptor regulation.

Type: Alanine-scanning mutagenesis with a receptor internalization readout

Experiment: Repeat the SERCA2a calcium-uptake and surface plasmon resonance experiments of PMID:27015675 with human AGTRAP and human ATP2A2, including a phospholamban competition arm, to establish whether the activity is conserved and whether the two regulators share a site.

Hypothesis: Human AGTRAP stimulates human SERCA2a as the mouse proteins do, and does so by competing with phospholamban for an overlapping site.

Type: Reconstituted calcium-uptake assay and surface plasmon resonance

Experiment: Retest a stratified sample of the two-hybrid partners in a membrane-compatible assay - split-ubiquitin, NanoBiT, or proximity labelling from AGTRAP in cells - sampling separately from the topologically accessible partners and from the 28 confined to the mitochondrial matrix, the nucleoplasm or the extracellular space. The second group is a built-in negative control, and the resulting hit rate would calibrate how much of this gene's binding record to believe.

Hypothesis: The large majority of AGTRAP's two-hybrid partners do not reproduce in a membrane-compatible assay, and the reproduction rate is far lower for partners confined to compartments its cytosolic tail cannot reach.

Type: Membrane-compatible interaction assay (split-ubiquitin / NanoBiT / proximity labelling)

Experiment: Determine whether AGTRAP acts on newly synthesised or on surface AT1 receptor by pulse-chase surface biotinylation in AGTRAP-knockout versus wild-type cells. Its steady-state pool is intracellular while its measured effect is on surface receptor number, and no published experiment distinguishes retention during delivery from accelerated retrieval.

Hypothesis: AGTRAP lowers surface AT1 receptor by accelerating retrieval from the plasma membrane rather than by retaining newly synthesised receptor intracellularly.

Type: Pulse-chase cell-surface biotinylation in a knockout background

Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGTRAP (human)

Current model (mechanistic narrative)

AGTRAP (ATRAP) is a multi-pass transmembrane protein that functions as a negative regulator of angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) signaling, binding specifically to the carboxyl-terminal cytoplasmic tail of the AT1a receptor and not to other G-protein-coupled receptors [PMID:10358057, PMID:12960423]. It localizes to the plasma membrane and to intracellular trafficking vesicles (ER, Golgi, endocytic vesicles), with constitutive translocation toward the plasma membrane; its cytoplasmic C-terminal domain is required for AT1R binding PMID:12960423. Through this interaction ATRAP promotes AT1R internalization and surface downregulation, thereby suppressing downstream AT1R-mediated signaling including phospholipase C activation, p38 MAPK, STAT3, and Akt, and attenuating angiotensin II-induced proliferative and hypertrophic responses in vascular smooth muscle cells and cardiomyocytes [PMID:10358057, PMID:11162453, PMID:15757644]. Genetic deletion in mice establishes ATRAP as a physiological negative regulator: Atrap-deficient animals show elevated blood pressure, increased plasma volume, and enhanced renal AT1R surface expression PMID:20093357, and additionally develop high-fat-diet-driven metabolic dysfunction that is rescued by transplantation of ATRAP-overexpressing adipose tissue PMID:23902639. Beyond AT1R, ATRAP interacts with the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase SERCA2a and enhances SERCA-dependent Ca2+ uptake to facilitate ventricular relaxation PMID:27015675. ATRAP abundance is tightly controlled post-translationally by proteasomal and immunoproteasomal degradation—notably via the immunoproteasome subunit β5i (PSMB8), whose action de-represses AT1R-driven NF-κB, NADPH oxidase, and TGF-β1/Smad signaling [PMID:25526681, PMID:30571551]—and post-transcriptionally by miR-125a/b-5p and miR-34a [PMID:37981211, PMID:41291382]. In cancer, ATRAP operates independently of AT1R, driving a USP14/PBX3/AKT-mTOR axis in breast cancer PMID:35414770 and an IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway in glioma PMID:41689202.

Overexpression of ATRAP in COS-7 cells markedly inhibited AT1a receptor-mediated activation of phospholipase C without affecting m3 receptor-mediated activation. 2003 High ATRAP is a transmembrane protein with three N-terminal hydrophobic domains (residues 14-36, 55-77, 88-108) and a hydrophilic C-terminal cytoplasmic tail (residues 109-161). Its N-terminus faces extracellularly, it localizes to intracellular trafficking vesicles (ER, Golgi, endocytic vesicles) and plasma membrane with constitutive translocation toward the plasma membrane. Notes

(AGTRAP-notes.md)

AGTRAP (ATRAP, Q6RW13) — review notes

Human gene, HGNC:13539, 159 aa, UniProt PE 1: Evidence at protein level.
PANTHER PTHR16521 / InterPro IPR009436 / Pfam PF06396, a single-subfamily
family (PTHR16521:SF3) with 1380 member proteins but only 5 Swiss-Prot
entries (human, mouse, rat, orangutan, Xenopus — all AGTRAP orthologues, no
paralogues). Reviewed-member counts from interpro/panther/PTHR16521/ are the
Swiss-Prot subset, not the family.

The shape of this gene's GO record

AGTRAP-goa.tsv has 199 rows. The fetch-gene stub seeded 199
existing_annotations entries, so nothing was collapsed here (unlike ACTR5 /
ADAMTSL5). Counts reconciled before review began:

wc -l < AGTRAP-goa.tsv        -> 200 (199 + header)
grep -c '^- term:' *-ai-review.yaml -> 199

Composition of the 199 rows:

rows content
187 GO:0005515 protein binding, IPI, IntAct
1 GO:0042802 identical protein binding, IPI (self, isoform 2)
3 UniProt SubCell IEAs (ER membrane, Golgi membrane, cytoplasmic vesicle membrane)
1 GO:0005794 Golgi apparatus, IDA, HPA
2 IBA (plasma membrane; regulation of blood pressure)
1 GO:0038166 angiotensin-activated signaling pathway, IEA from InterPro
4 Ensembl Compara IEAs (GO:0004945, GO:0001666, GO:0005886, GO:0005938)

So 94% of this gene's GO record is protein binding, and the interaction
that the gene is named for — AGTR1 — is not in it at all.

Finding 1: GO:0004945 angiotensin type II receptor activity is a symbol confusion amplified by orthology projection

The human row is enables GO:0004945, IEA (ECO:0000265, GO_REF:0000107,
Ensembl Compara) with UniProtKB:Q9WVK0 = mouse Agtrap (Swiss-Prot,
ATRAP_MOUSE, a true 1:1 orthologue — resolved, not assumed).

Going one level deeper than the donor (QuickGO,
geneProductId=UniProtKB:Q9WVK0): mouse Agtrap holds GO:0004945 by IMP from
PMID:10425188, assigned by MGI. That paper is "Increased vasoconstrictor
response of the mouse lacking angiotensin II type 2 receptor" — an Agtr2
knockout study. Its abstract never mentions Agtrap/ATRAP.

Querying by reference rather than by gene makes the mechanism explicit:

QuickGO annotation/search?reference=PMID:10425188  -> 13 annotations, 3 entities
  Agt    (P11859)  5 rows
  Agtr2  (P35374)  5 rows  incl. GO:0004945 enables IGI   <- the correct holder
  Agtrap (Q9WVK0)  2 rows  incl. GO:0004945 enables IMP   <- the confusion

Agtr2 and Agtrap both received GO:0004945 from the same paper. Only one of
them is an angiotensin receptor.

Independent of provenance, the term is biologically false for this protein:

  • GO:0004945 is defined as "An angiotensin receptor activity that acts via Gi
    protein coupling and cGMP (NO) generation"    . AGTRAP is a 159-aa protein with
    three TM helices (UniProt FT 24-44, 56-76, 87-107), not a 7TM GPCR, and
    has no G-protein coupling anywhere in its record.
  • The gene's founding paper tested exactly this and excluded it:
    PMID:10358057 — "ATRAP interacts specifically with the carboxyl-terminal
    domain of the AT1a receptor but not with those of angiotensin II type 2 (AT2),
    m3 muscarinic acetylcholine, bradykinin B2, endothelin B, and
    beta2-adrenergic receptors."

So the annotation asserts, of the protein named for the type-1 receptor, an
activity of the type-2 receptor that was experimentally excluded for it.
Action: REMOVE.

The error has spread to three species. Rat Agtrap (Q642A2) carries
GO:0004945 twice — by Ensembl IEA and by RGD ISO — so human, rat and mouse
all currently assert it. Fixing the MGI row would clear all three.

Finding 2: GO:0008217 regulation of blood pressure — right term, wrong evidence

The human row is IBA from PANTHER:PTN002703102 + MGI:MGI:1339977. The PAINT
file (interpro/panther/PTHR16521/PTHR16521-paint.tsv) shows the family has
exactly two IBD annotations, both seeded from mouse Agtrap alone:

PTHR16521  PTN002314244  GO:0005886  C  IBD  MGI:MGI:1339977  taxon:6072
PTHR16521  PTN002703102  GO:0008217  P  IBD  MGI:MGI:1339977  taxon:117571

and mouse Agtrap's only experimental GO:0008217 row is the same
PMID:10425188 IMP from Finding 1. So the chain human IBA -> PAINT node ->
mouse IMP terminates in a paper about a different gene.

The conclusion nevertheless survives on evidence nobody curated: PMID:20093357
(Oppermann/Castrop, JASN 2010) — "Mean systolic BP was significantly higher in
Atrap-/- mice compared with wild-type mice." Kept as KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
(organism-level physiology downstream of AT1R restraint, not AGTRAP's own
molecular function), with a suggested_question asking MGI to re-reference.

This is the inverse of the usual campaign finding: the propagation is sound and
the donor's citation is the defect.

Finding 3: GO:0001666 response to hypoxia rests on one rat IEP

Human row: IEA from rat Q642A2 (Swiss-Prot ATRAP_RAT, true orthologue).
Rat's own evidence: a single IEP from PMID:17033689, "Vascular response to
hypoxic preconditioning in the immature brain". That reference annotates
exactly 2 entities in all of GOA (rat Agtrap and Angptl4), both IEP — i.e. a
transcript-abundance change in neonatal rat brain. Same shape as AFF4's
GO:0034976. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED.

Finding 4: 94% of the interaction record is one assay class, and the informative partners are in the other one

IntAct (/intact/ws/interaction/findInteractions/Q6RW13, all 617 evidences
retrieved; len(results) == totalElements asserted):

publication evidences methods
PMID:32296183 (HuRI) 276 validated two hybrid 92 + two hybrid array 92 + two hybrid prey pooling approach 92
PMID:25416956 (HI-II-14) 202 68 + 67 + 67, same three sub-methods
21 others 139 mostly Y2H; 27 anti tag coip, 3 BioID, 2 anti bait coip, 1 crosslink, 1 CLASH

92 x 3 and ~68 x 3 is the arithmetic of one screen logged three ways. This
is the NbExp=3 artefact (ACRV1, ADAMTSL5) confirmed by exact counts rather
than inferred: UniProt's NbExp=3 for most AGTRAP partners is one experiment.
Overall 583/617 = 94.5% of evidences are two-hybrid, and only 23 of 213
distinct pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method.

The GOA import is drawn entirely from the Y2H side: all 188 binding rows trace
to 9 CCSB-lineage publications. Partner accessions resolved (132 distinct; all
resolved, entryType.startswith("UniProtKB reviewed") used so TrEMBL is not
silently promoted): 121 Swiss-Prot, 11 TrEMBL, and several TrEMBL ones are
partial ORFeome clones rather than the canonical protein —

GOA partner length canonical
A0A0S2Z3E9 "FGA" 84 aa P02671 866 aa
A0A0S2Z4D9 "GAD1" 111 aa Q99259 594 aa
Q96AL5 "PBX3" 367 aa P40426 434 aa
Q5JS98 "PBX3" 455 aa P40426 434 aa
Q7L1H2 "STAG3L1" 79 aa —

Topology check (scratchpad/topology.py): AGTRAP's only substantial
cytosol-facing surface is TOPO_DOM 108-159 — 52 residues, 20 of them
disordered. Of the 131 non-self GOA partners, 28 are confined to the
mitochondrial matrix/inner membrane, the nucleoplasm, or the extracellular
space and cannot reach that surface; 17 more are mixed; 67 are cytosol-facing;
19 have no recorded location. Reported as it came out — this is a supporting
argument, not the decisive one, because a majority of partners are nominally
accessible. The decisive argument is the assay structure above.

The property that every screen row's verdict rests on, stated exactly. An
earlier draft said, on all 178 rows, that "searching this partner independently
of the AGTRAP symbol found no follow-up study". I did not run 131 separate
partner searches, so that was an over-claim, and it was replaced by what was
actually measured (scratchpad/nony2h_vs_goa.py, which asserts
len(results) == totalElements and then asserts the property per partner):

GOA partner accessions (base): 132
GOA partners with no IntAct record under Q6RW13: 0
IntAct partners with any non-two-hybrid method: 23
   of those, present in GOA: 0
ASSERTION HELD: every GOA partner found in IntAct has two-hybrid methods only

Every one of the 132 GOA partners resolves in IntAct, every one is
two-hybrid-only, and the 23 partners that do have orthogonal support are
disjoint from the GOA set.

The contrast is the finding. The 23 pairs with non-Y2H (AP-MS / co-IP /
BioID) evidence are almost all membrane proteins — CYB5D2, ENPP6, MBLAC2,
TMEM47, TMEM106B, LAMP5, SLC15A3, SLC15A4, TMEM63A, CFTR, CHRNB1, SLC1A1,
SLC18A2, PAFAH2, TNFRSF10C — a coherent ER/endolysosomal membrane neighbourhood
for a 3-TM ER/Golgi protein. None of them is in GOA. GOA imported the assay
class whose partners are largely implausible and none of the class whose
partners fit the protein's own cell biology.

A count that refused to add up, and what it turned out to be

First draft of the PMID:16189514 reference note said "3 binding rows". The TSV has
2. The 3 was an IntAct evidence count, and the extra evidence is a canonical
Q6RW13-Q6RW13 self-pair that GOA did not import. Chasing it corrected a
second claim: the GO:0042802 row had been written as a self-interaction "detected
once, in the HuRI screen", which is true of the GOA row and false of IntAct —
PMID:16189514 and PMID:25416956 also report a canonical self-pair. All three are
the same CCSB clone collection in the same two-hybrid system, so the verdict
(MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED) is unchanged, but it now rests on "recurrence on one
platform, never tested by another method" rather than on "seen once", which was
simply wrong.

Per-reference GOA binding-row counts, re-derived from the TSV rather than from prose:
32296183 91 (90 + the self row) · 25416956 66 · 31515488 10 · 26871637 8 ·
21516116 4 · 25910212 3 · 16189514 2 · 19060904 2 · 29892012 2 = 188.

Three Y2H partners that survive scrutiny

Searching the partners rather than the symbol (the recall gap affinage cannot
close) turned up orthogonal validation for three. "Three" is what this search
found, not a proof that no fourth exists — the exhaustive statement available is
the IntAct one above, that no GOA partner has non-two-hybrid evidence:

  • PITPNC1 / RdgBβ (Q9UKF7, 4 GOA rows) — PMID:21728994, titled for
    RdgBβ, not for AGTRAP: "the PITP domain of RdgBβ interacts with the integral
    membrane protein ATRAP ... causing membrane recruitment"    . This is the one
    partner that yields an informative MF for AGTRAP itself: it is the membrane
    anchor. MODIFY -> GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity (a term
    already used for integral-membrane tethers such as SUN1/SUN2 and GPR179).
  • FAM114A1 (Q8IWE2, 1 GOA row) — PMID:35671117, titled for FAM114A1.
    It explicitly starts from the Y2H hit and validates it: "we validated the
    interaction between AGTRAP and FAM114A1 in mouse heart lysates and cultured
    PMCFs by IP and Western blotting"    . KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.
  • PBX3 (Q96AL5 / Q5JS98, 4 GOA rows) — PMID:35414770: "we performed
    co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged ATRAP,
    which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3"    . Corroborated but in a
    breast-cancer over-expression context, and both GOA accessions are unreviewed
    non-canonical clones. KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.

The remaining 178 GO:0005515 rows and the GO:0042802 self-row get
MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED — not REMOVE, matching the ADAMTSL5 precedent for
comparable unreplicated Y2H rows (and diverging deliberately from ADAMTSL4's
REMOVE; the divergence is flagged rather than silent).

Finding 5: the gene's defining interaction is absent from human GOA

AGTR1 binding is measured, curated by UniProt on the human entry
(SUBUNIT: Interacts with RACK1, and with the C-terminal region of AGTR1.,
ECO:0000269|PubMed:11733189, ECO:0000269|PubMed:12960423), given a feature
(FT REGION 110..122 /note="Interaction with AGTR1"), and present as
GO:0005515 IPI with P29754 (mouse Agtr1a) on the mouse orthologue — yet
it is nowhere in the human GO record.

GO:0031702 type 1 angiotensin receptor binding exists and is exactly right
(Daviet showed the binding is AT1a-specific and excludes AT2). Proposed as NEW.

A claim I had to retract here. The first draft said its 197 holders were all
angiotensinogen orthologues by IEA — read off page 1 of a paginated QuickGO result,
which is exactly the failure the brief warns about. Paging the whole thing (197
annotations over 188 gene products, len(results) asserted against numberOfHits)
gives 175 IEA, 10 ISO, 9 IPI, 3 IDA, and 16 entities with non-IEA evidence:

holder evidence what it binds
AGT human IPI, mouse IDA, rat ISO the ligand precursor
ARRB2 rat IPI, mouse ISO receptor cytoplasmic face
JAK2 rat IPI, mouse ISO/IEA receptor cytoplasmic face
TYK2 rat IPI, mouse ISO receptor cytoplasmic face
ARAP1 rat IPI, mouse ISO receptor cytoplasmic face
BDKRB2, EDNRB human/rat IPI, ISO heteromeric receptor partners

So the term is already used for cytoplasmic-face binders — AGTRAP's exact class —
which makes the proposal stronger than the retracted version claimed, not weaker. What
is genuinely thin is human coverage: five human entities, only AGT and BDKRB2 by IPI,
the rest Ensembl projections.

Note the composite-claim trap in UniProt's SUBUNIT line: the RACK1 half comes
from PMID:11733189 and the AGTR1 half from PMID:12960423. PMID:11733189
reports the human AGTRAP-RACK1 interaction (Y2H + GST pull-down + co-IP +
SPR) and does not itself assay AGTR1. Cited accordingly.

RACK1 (P63244) is likewise absent from GOA despite four orthogonal assays on
the human protein. Recorded as a coverage gap, not proposed as a bare
protein binding row.

Finding 6: GO:0038166 asserts pathway membership where the data show negative regulation

The row is IEA from InterPro:IPR009436 — the AGTRAP family signature, i.e. a
term derived from the family's name. Every functional measurement on this
protein runs the other way: PLC inhibition (PMID:10358057), reduced inositol
lipids / c-fos / proliferation (PMID:12960423), elevated BP and increased
surface AT1R on knockout (PMID:20093357). GO keeps regulation terms outside
the process they regulate, so MODIFY -> GO:0110062 negative regulation of angiotensin-activated signaling pathway, which carries the direction the data
actually support.

Finding 7: a second, AT1R-independent molecular activity

PMID:27015675 (titled for SERCA2a, not for AGTRAP): pull-down + MALDI-MS,
co-IP and SPR place Atrap on the cardiac Ca2+-ATPase SERCA2a, and "Atrap
enhanced the SERCA-dependent Ca(2+) uptake in isolated SR membrane vesicles";
Atrap-/- myocytes show prolonged Ca2+-transient decay and the mice a reduced
maximum ventricular filling rate. All of it is mouse, so proposed for human as
ISS: GO:0141109 transporter activator activity, the sibling of
GO:0141110 transporter inhibitor activity that phospholamban holds by IDA.
Not in GOA in any form.

Finding 8: the coverage gap is symmetric, and mouse shows it is fixable

Every finding above looks at AGTRAP's own record. Querying each partner's GO
record instead (scratchpad/reciprocity.py, paging asserted against
numberOfHits) shows the missing curation is not a quirk of this gene's entry —
the targeted papers produced nothing on either side:

paper partner annotations from that paper on the partner
PMID:12960423 human AGTR1 P30556 0 of 79
PMID:11733189 human RACK1 P63244 0 of 166
PMID:21728994 human PITPNC1 Q9UKF7 0 of 28
PMID:27015675 human ATP2A2 P16615 0 of 84
PMID:35414770 human PBX3 P40426 0 of 23
PMID:35671117 mouse Fam114a1 Q9D281 10, incl. reciprocal GO:0005515 IPI with Q9WVK0

Five targeted interaction papers, ten opportunities across both partners, zero
human annotations. The single counter-example is the one that matters: MGI
curated PMID:35671117 reciprocally — mouse Fam114a1 IPI with Q9WVK0 and
mouse Agtrap IPI with Q9D281 — and also gave Fam114a1 GO:0038166 by IMP. So
the same paper yields a curated, reciprocal, experimentally-grounded pair in
mouse and nothing at all in human.

Two consequences worth stating. First, this is a curation defect rather than
a biology one, which is the distinction AFF4's review drew; the diagnosis for
AGTRAP is "uncharacterised in GO", not "over-annotated", even though 181 rows are
marked over-annotated — those two coexist here because the 188 screen rows and
the missing targeted rows come from different places. Second, human AGTRAP's only
GO:0038166 row is an InterPro family-name mapping, while mouse Fam114a1 — its
partner — holds GO:0038166 by IMP. The experimental grounding for
angiotensin-signalling involvement exists in the neighbourhood; it just never
reached this gene.

The three PITPNC1 back-references that do exist on the partner side
(PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956, all IntAct GO:0005515 IPI)
are the same CCSB screens already counted here — reciprocity of the screen, not
of the targeted study.

Round 2: MeSH organism indexing settles a species question the abstracts do not

The reviewer flagged a real internal inconsistency: GO:0031702 was coded IPI
on PMID:12960423 while GO:0002092 was coded ISS on PMID:11162453
"because the abstracts do not state the species" — the same situation, two
different codes. And it added a fact I had seen and failed to act on: that
abstract numbers the protein 14-36 / 55-77 / 88-108 with a cytoplasmic tail at
109-161, and 161 aa is mouse Agtrap, not the 159-aa human protein.

The tiebreaker neither of us had used is NLM's own MeSH organism indexing,
which discriminates these papers cleanly:

paper MeSH organism terms used for
PMID:12960423 Humans — no Animals, no Mice GO:0031702 IPI
PMID:10358057 Animals, Mice — no Humans corroboration only
PMID:11162453 Animals, Rats — no Humans GO:0002092 ISS
PMID:15757644 Animals, Mice — no Humans corroboration only
PMID:27015675 Animals, Humans, HEK293 Cells GO:0141109 ISS

Reproduce the table with one call (the cached publications/PMID_*.md records
carry title, authors and abstract but no MeSH headings, so this cannot be
checked from the repo alone — worth capturing in the cache now that the indexing
has done real curatorial work here):

# Per-PMID, because the load-bearing entries are ABSENCES: a single efetch over
# all five ids yields an unattributed union in which 'Animals' appears (from the
# other four papers), so a merged query cannot show that 12960423 lacks it.
for id in 12960423 10358057 11162453 15757644 27015675; do
  printf 'PMID:%s\t' "$id"
  curl -s "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=pubmed&id=$id&retmode=xml" \
    | grep -o '<DescriptorName[^>]*>[^<]*</DescriptorName>' \
    | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g' \
    | grep -Ex 'Humans|Animals|Mice|Rats|HEK293 Cells' \
    | paste -sd, -
  sleep 1
done

Output when run (this is the table above, and it was run before being recorded):

PMID:12960423   Humans
PMID:10358057   Animals,Mice
PMID:11162453   Animals,Rats
PMID:15757644   Animals,Mice
PMID:27015675   Animals,HEK293 Cells,Humans

So the two codes are consistent once the indexing is consulted rather than the
abstract alone: 12960423 is indexed as human work, 11162453 as rat work. NLM
essentially always adds Animals when animal material is used, so its absence
from 12960423 is meaningful, and it agrees with UniProt's ECO:0000269 on the
human entry.

This does not dissolve the numbering conflict, and the review now says so in
the row rather than leaving it to be found. The likeliest reconciliation is that
the authors kept the residue numbering of the sequence first published in
PMID:10358057 while working with human constructs — but PMC284805 yields no
extractable full text (XML restricted, HTML empty, no PDF link), so it cannot be
confirmed. IPI is retained on explicit deference to the curator, with the
condition stated: if the full text shows rodent constructs, the code becomes
ISS with Q9WVK0 and only the code changes, not the term.

PMID:27015675 cuts the other way and is recorded as such: it carries Humans
and HEK293 Cells alongside Animals, so the SERCA2a binding measurements may
have used human constructs even though the calcium-uptake and knockout work did
not. ISS is the conservative reading there, flagged for revisiting.

Also from round 2: both ISS rows transfer from a mouse orthologue that holds
neither term, i.e. ISS from nothing. Rather than silently recode them, the mouse-
side annotations they should descend from are now requested explicitly in
suggested_questions, and the GO:0043495 differentia problem is filed as an
ontology request rather than left as a per-gene caveat. The PITPNC1 rows now say
why that membrane-anchoring activity is deliberately not elevated to a core
function — one PMA-dependent experiment, no measured consequence for AGTRAP
itself — which the PR body had described as "the anchor" without the review ever
saying so.

Checks run that came back negative (recorded so the next reviewer knows)

  • Retractions / errata / expressions of concern: all 21 PMIDs relied on were
    checked via CommentsCorrections/RefType on each cited article's own PubMed
    record and publication types. None is retracted, corrected, or under an
    expression of concern; the only hits are three benign CommentIn entries
    (25416956, 25910212, 26871637).
  • Paralogue transfer: PTHR16521 contains no paralogues — all 5 reviewed
    members are AGTRAP orthologues — so WRONG_ORTHOLOG_OR_PARALOG does not apply
    to any row here. Both Compara donors (Q9WVK0 mouse, Q642A2 rat) and the
    PAINT seed (MGI:MGI:1339977) are true orthologues.
  • Dead/obsolete accessions: all 132 GOA partner accessions resolved to live
    UniProt entries with a gene name, as did both distinct UniProtKB:
    WITH/FROM accessions on the 11 non-binding rows — Q9WVK0 (3 rows) and
    Q642A2 (1 row). (An earlier draft of this line said "all 4 WITH/FROM protein
    accessions", conflating 4 rows with 4 accessions; there are 2. The
    O15507 failure mode from ACTR10 — a dead accession that answers every query
    with a silent zero — is absent here.)
  • IBA landing above its donor (ACRV1 pattern): mouse Agtrap holds
    GO:0005886 plasma membrane by IDA and the human IBA is at the same term, so
    no downward MODIFY is warranted.
  • Sibling-review inconsistency: no paralogue reviews exist to cross-check;
    the nearest precedent is the treatment of CCSB Y2H rows in ADAMTSL5 (followed)
    vs ADAMTSL4 (diverged from, deliberately, and said so).

affinage recall

gates_passed: True, faith_pct: 100, 21 citations, all numeric PMIDs, no
bioRxiv-style ids. It supplied the decisive partner-titled papers
(PMID:21728994, PMID:27015675, PMID:35414770) — better recall than this
campaign's 52% average. It missed PMID:35671117 (FAM114A1, the only
orthogonal validation of a HuRI hit) and PMID:10425188 / PMID:17033689, the
two donor references that turned out to carry the review's biggest findings.
Neither of the latter is findable from an AGTRAP-keyed literature search; both
came from querying donor evidence in QuickGO.

Scripts

Reproducible helpers used for this review live in the session scratchpad, not in
the repo, because they are one-off queries against live services rather than
analyses whose outputs are committed: partners.py (resolve every WITH/FROM
partner, assert 199 GOA rows and 0 unresolved accessions), topology.py
(compartment classification), intact2.py (IntAct evidence/method/publication
tabulation with a len(results) == totalElements assertion).

description: 'AGTRAP (ATRAP) is a small, ubiquitously expressed integral membrane protein of 159
  amino acids with three transmembrane helices, an extracellular/lumenal N-terminus and a roughly
  50-residue cytoplasmic C-terminal tail. It sits in endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and endocytic
  vesicle membranes and at the plasma membrane, and its vesicles move constitutively toward the
  cell surface. Its defining activity is binding the carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic tail of the type-1
  angiotensin II receptor (AGTR1) through its own C-terminal tail; the interaction is selective
  for AT1 and does not extend to the AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin B2, endothelin B or beta2-adrenergic
  receptors. Through it AGTRAP restrains angiotensin II signalling: it promotes AT1 receptor internalization
  and lowers receptor density at the cell surface, and cells over-expressing it show reduced phospholipase
  C activation, inositol lipid generation, c-fos induction and proliferation in response to angiotensin
  II. Mice lacking Atrap have elevated arterial blood pressure, expanded plasma volume and increased
  surface AT1 receptor in the renal cortex, where the protein is most abundant in the proximal tubule
  brush border; human AGTRAP mRNA is highest in kidney, heart, pancreas and thyroid. In heart, AGTRAP
  additionally binds the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2a and stimulates its calcium
  uptake, accelerating cytosolic calcium decay and ventricular relaxation - an activity independent
  of the angiotensin receptor. Further reported partners include the scaffold RACK1, the phosphatidylinositol
  transfer protein PITPNC1/RdgB-beta, which AGTRAP recruits to membranes, and FAM114A1. AGTRAP is
  itself neither a receptor nor an enzyme: it has no G-protein coupling and no catalytic activity.'

    reason: 'The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP,
      which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP
      domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly
      GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - ''brings together a protein ... with a membrane
      ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein'' - which integral membrane tethers
      such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what
      AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than
      left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495''s differentia describes the adaptor as reaching
      the membrane ''either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein'',
      and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO''s usage is broader
      than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins
      tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even
      where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and
      the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956,
      PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of
      core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the
      recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels,
      is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it
      was measured, rather than promoted.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0043495
      label: protein-membrane adaptor activity
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:21728994
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:21728994
      supporting_text: interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I
        receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment
- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:19060904
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q96AL5
  review:
    summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer
      cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted,
      and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer
      lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats
      keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a
      nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments
      do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q96AL5, an unreviewed 367-aa TrEMBL entry,
      not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein.
      Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of
      the screen set has.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:35414770
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:35414770
      supporting_text: we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged
        ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:21516116
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:O00330
  review:
    summary: PDHX (O00330) appears only as a yeast two-hybrid hit, in 3 CCSB interactome releases
      (PMID:21516116, PMID:25416956, PMID:31515488) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal
      experiment supports it and protein binding conveys no molecular function, so the row is marked
      over-annotated rather than treated as evidence about AGTRAP.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications
      that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617
      evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 =
      92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array
      / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same
      way, so UniProt''s NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct
      pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed
      as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane
      protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20
      of them disordered. PDHX is confined to the mitochondrial matrix, which that 52-residue cytosolic
      surface cannot reach in an intact cell. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair.
      That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP''s 132 GOA partners
      is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or
      BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP
      appears in the affinage record or in UniProt''s curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either.
      That is the distinction drawn across this gene''s binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3
      each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE,
      matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review
      (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).'

      protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20
      of them disordered. TFAM is confined to the mitochondrial matrix, which that 52-residue cytosolic
      surface cannot reach in an intact cell. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair.
      That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP''s 132 GOA partners
      is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or
      BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP
      appears in the affinage record or in UniProt''s curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either.
      That is the distinction drawn across this gene''s binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3
      each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE,
      matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review
      (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).'

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:25416956
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q5JS98
  review:
    summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer
      cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted,
      and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer
      lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats
      keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a
      nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments
      do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q5JS98, an unreviewed 455-aa TrEMBL entry,
      not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein.
      Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of
      the screen set has.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:35414770
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:35414770
      supporting_text: we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged
        ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:25416956
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q8IWE2
  review:
    summary: FAM114A1 is a two-hybrid hit that a later targeted study took up and confirmed in native
      tissue, placing the AGTRAP-FAM114A1 pair upstream of AT1R abundance in cardiac fibroblasts.
      Kept, but protein binding is not a core function.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: PMID:35671117 is titled for FAM114A1, not for AGTRAP, and states outright that it began
      from the published two-hybrid candidates and then validated this one by immunoprecipitation
      and Western blotting in mouse heart lysates and primary cardiac fibroblasts - i.e. an orthogonal
      assay at endogenous levels, which none of the other screen partners has. Loss of Fam114a1
      raised AGTRAP protein and lowered AT1R, and siRNA knockdown of Agtrap reversed the Fam114a1-null
      phenotype, so the interaction is functional as well as physical. Retained as non-core because
      GO:0005515 itself conveys no molecular function and the regulatory direction runs from FAM114A1
      onto AGTRAP rather than the reverse.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:35671117
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:35671117
      supporting_text: we validated the interaction between AGTRAP and FAM114A1 in mouse heart lysates
        and cultured PMCFs by IP and Western blotting
- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:25416956
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q8IWL3
  review:
    summary: HSCB (Q8IWL3) appears only as a yeast two-hybrid hit, in 2 CCSB interactome releases
      (PMID:25416956, PMID:31515488) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal experiment
      supports it and protein binding conveys no molecular function, so the row is marked over-annotated
      rather than treated as evidence about AGTRAP.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications
      that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617
      evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 =
      92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array
      / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same
      way, so UniProt''s NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct
      pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed
      as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane
      protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20
      of them disordered. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression:
      across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP''s 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and
      the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint
      from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP appears in the affinage record
      or in UniProt''s curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either. That is the distinction drawn
      across this gene''s binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay;
      this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable
      unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4,
      which used REMOVE).'
