- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:25416956
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9UKF7
  review:
    summary: 'PITPNC1 (RdgB-beta) is one of only three AGTRAP two-hybrid partners with orthogonal
      support, and the only one that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself:
      a targeted study shows AGTRAP recruits the PITP domain of RdgB-beta to membranes, i.e. AGTRAP
      is the membrane anchor.'
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP,
      which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP
      domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly
      GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - ''brings together a protein ... with a membrane
      ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein'' - which integral membrane tethers
      such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what
      AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than
      left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495''s differentia describes the adaptor as reaching
      the membrane ''either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein'',
      and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO''s usage is broader
      than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins
      tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even
      where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and
      the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956,
      PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of
      core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the
      recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels,
      is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it
      was measured, rather than promoted.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0043495
      label: protein-membrane adaptor activity
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:21728994
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:21728994
      supporting_text: interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I
        receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment

      (PMID:32296183) drawn from one clone set and one assay. No orthogonal experiment supports

    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'All 188 GOA binding rows for AGTRAP come from nine CCSB binary-interactome publications
      that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617
      evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 =
      92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array
      / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same
      way, so UniProt''s NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct
      pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed
      as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane
      protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20
      of them disordered. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods only for this pair. That is not an impression:
      across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP''s 132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and
      the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation or BioID support are disjoint

      across this gene''s binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3 each have an orthogonal assay;
      this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE, matching the treatment of comparable
      unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4,
      which used REMOVE).'

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:32296183
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q96AL5
  isoform: Q6RW13-2
  review:
    summary: PBX3 is a two-hybrid hit later corroborated by co-immunoprecipitation in breast cancer
      cells, where AGTRAP directs USP14-mediated stabilisation of PBX3. Real but context-restricted,
      and the accession used is not canonical PBX3.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: PMID:35414770 independently co-immunoprecipitates ATRAP with PBX3 in two breast cancer
      lines and shows ATRAP over-expression raises PBX3 protein without changing its mRNA. Two caveats
      keep this non-core. First, the assay is over-expression in a cancer context and PBX3 is a
      nuclear homeodomain factor, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass membrane protein - the compartments
      do not obviously meet. Second, the GOA row cites Q96AL5, an unreviewed 367-aa TrEMBL entry,
      not canonical PBX3 (P40426, 434 aa), so the clone assayed is not the full-length protein.
      Kept rather than removed because an orthogonal assay exists, which is more than the rest of
      the screen set has.
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:35414770
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:35414770
      supporting_text: we performed co-IP assays in MDA-MB-453 and T47D cells transfected with Flag-tagged
        ATRAP, which revealed that ATRAP can directly bind with PBX3

- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:32296183
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9UKF7-2
  isoform: Q6RW13-2
  review:
    summary: 'PITPNC1 (RdgB-beta) is one of only three AGTRAP two-hybrid partners with orthogonal
      support, and the only one that yields an informative molecular function for AGTRAP itself:
      a targeted study shows AGTRAP recruits the PITP domain of RdgB-beta to membranes, i.e. AGTRAP
      is the membrane anchor.'
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The partner is real. PMID:21728994 is titled for RdgB-beta rather than for AGTRAP,
      which is why no AGTRAP-keyed search surfaces it; it reports that on PMA treatment the PITP
      domain of RdgB-beta engages AGTRAP and is thereby recruited to membranes. That is exactly
      GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity - ''brings together a protein ... with a membrane
      ... to establish or maintain the localization of the protein'' - which integral membrane tethers
      such as SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 already carry. Bare protein binding states nothing about what
      AGTRAP does, so the row is modified rather than accepted. Two caveats, stated rather than
      left for a reader to find. First, GO:0043495''s differentia describes the adaptor as reaching
      the membrane ''either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein'',
      and AGTRAP does neither - it is itself the integral membrane protein. GO''s usage is broader
      than that wording: SUN1, SUN2 and GPR179 all hold the term and are all integral membrane proteins
      tethering a partner at a membrane, which is exactly this case, so the term fits practice even
      where the differentia reads narrowly. Second, the recruitment rests on a single paper, and
      the underlying GOA evidence here is still two-hybrid (PMID:16189514, PMID:19060904, PMID:25416956,
      PMID:32296183, 4 CCSB releases of one clone set). This activity is deliberately kept out of
      core_functions: a single PMA-dependent recruitment experiment, with no consequence of the
      recruitment measured for AGTRAP itself and no evidence that it happens at endogenous levels,
      is a real molecular function but not a demonstrated core one. It is recorded here, where it
      was measured, rather than promoted.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0043495
      label: protein-membrane adaptor activity
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:21728994
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:21728994
      supporting_text: interacts with the integral membrane protein ATRAP (angiotensin II type I
        receptor-associated protein; also known as AGTRAP) causing membrane recruitment

      that share one ORFeome clone collection and one yeast two-hybrid system. IntAct holds 617
      evidences for Q6RW13, of which 583 (94.5%) are two-hybrid; PMID:32296183 contributes 276 =
      92 pairs logged under exactly three sub-method terms (validated two hybrid / two hybrid array
      / two hybrid prey pooling approach) and PMID:25416956 contributes 202 = 68/67/67 the same
      way, so UniProt''s NbExp counts sub-methods, not experiments. Only 23 of 213 distinct IntAct
      pairs carry any non-two-hybrid method, and none of those 23 is in GOA. Both partners are over-expressed
      as fusions in the yeast nucleus, whereas AGTRAP is a three-pass ER/Golgi/vesicle membrane
      protein whose only substantial cytosol-facing surface is residues 108-159 - 52 residues, 20
      of them disordered. POLDIP2 is confined to the mitochondrial matrix and nucleus, which that
      52-residue cytosolic surface cannot reach in an intact cell. IntAct holds two-hybrid methods
      only for this pair. That is not an impression: across all 617 evidences, every one of AGTRAP''s
      132 GOA partners is two-hybrid-only, and the 23 AGTRAP pairs that do carry AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation
      or BioID support are disjoint from the GOA set. No targeted study of this partner with AGTRAP
      appears in the affinage record or in UniProt''s curated SUBUNIT and FUNCTION lines either.
      That is the distinction drawn across this gene''s binding rows: PITPNC1, FAM114A1 and PBX3
      each have an orthogonal assay; this pair has none. MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED rather than REMOVE,
      matching the treatment of comparable unreplicated CCSB rows in the merged ADAMTSL5 review
      (and deliberately diverging from ADAMTSL4, which used REMOVE).'

- term:
    id: GO:0005789
    label: endoplasmic reticulum membrane
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000044
  qualifier: located_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0097
  review:
    summary: Correct. UniProt's endoplasmic reticulum membrane SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line for AGTRAP
      carries ECO:0000269|PubMed:12960423, so this keyword-derived row traces to a direct microscopy
      result on the protein rather than to a prediction.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: PubMed:12960423 localised ATRAP by immunofluorescence and electron microscopy to perinuclear
      vesicular membranes corresponding to endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and endocytic vesicles,
      and this is the experimental basis of the three UniProt SubCell terms. The protein is a multi-pass
      membrane protein (three predicted TM helices, UniProt FT 24-44, 56-76, 87-107), so a membrane-qualified
      location is the right granularity.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: colocalization analysis by immunofluorescence shows that ATRAP colocalizes
        in an intracellular vesicular compartment corresponding to endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi,
        and endocytic vesicles
- term:
    id: GO:0005794
    label: Golgi apparatus
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000052
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Independent immunofluorescence confirmation of the Golgi localisation, from the Human
      Protein Atlas rather than from the UniProt keyword route.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: This is the only IDA in AGTRAP's entire GO record and it agrees with the experimental
      Golgi localisation curated from PubMed:12960423. It is less precise than the GO:0000139 Golgi
      membrane row already present, but it is independent evidence for the same compartment rather
      than a redundant transfer, so it is kept as annotated.
- term:
    id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  evidence_type: IBA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000033
  qualifier: is_active_in
  supporting_entities:
  - MGI:MGI:1339977
  - PANTHER:PTN002314244
  review:
    summary: Sound. The single PAINT node carrying this term is seeded from mouse Agtrap, whose
      own evidence is an IDA at the same term, and the human protein is independently reported at
      the plasma membrane.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: 'PTHR16521 has exactly two IBD annotations family-wide and this is one of them (node
      PTN002314244, seed MGI:MGI:1339977, taxon:6072). Querying the donor''s own evidence rather
      than only its identity: mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0) holds GO:0005886 by IDA from PubMed:10358057,
      assigned by UniProt - so the propagation does not land above its donor and no downward MODIFY
      is warranted (the ACRV1 failure mode was checked for and is absent). PubMed:12960423 independently
      reports the human protein at the plasma membrane with constitutive vesicular translocation
      towards it, which is also where AGTR1 engagement must occur, so is_active_in is apt.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: Real-time tracking of ATRAP vesicles shows constitutive translocation toward
        the plasma membrane.
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_CORE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: MGI:MGI:1339977
        source_label: mouse Agtrap
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Holds GO:0005886 by IDA from PubMed:10358057; a true 1:1 orthologue, not a paralogue
          - PTHR16521 contains no paralogues.
      - source_id: PANTHER:PTN002314244
        source_label: PTHR16521 Eumetazoa node
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Internal tree node, not a protein; one of only two IBD annotations in the whole
          family.
- term:
    id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
  qualifier: located_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000030865
  review:
    summary: 'Redundant with the IBA row but independently sound: the Compara donor is mouse Agtrap,
      which holds plasma membrane by its own IDA.'
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: 'The donor UniProtKB:Q9WVK0 was resolved (ATRAP_MOUSE, Swiss-Prot, 161 aa) and its own
      annotations queried: GO:0005886 located_in by IDA from PubMed:10358057. Unlike the GO:0004945

      annotated.'
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_CORE
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
        source_label: mouse Agtrap (ATRAP_MOUSE)
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Reviewed (Swiss-Prot) 1:1 orthologue; carries GO:0005886 located_in by IDA from
          PubMed:10358057.
- term:
    id: GO:0005938
    label: cell cortex
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000107
  qualifier: located_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
  - ensembl:ENSMUSP00000030865
  review:
    summary: Over-annotated. The donor's own IDA is a light-microscopy peripheral-staining call
      on mouse Agtrap; for an integral multi-pass membrane protein the plasma membrane term already
      annotated is the apt one, and cell cortex adds a sub-membranous cytoplasmic claim the protein
      does not occupy.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'The donor was resolved and its evidence queried: mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0) holds GO:0005938
      located_in by IDA from PubMed:10358057, the same fluorescence-microscopy experiment that supports
      its plasma membrane IDA. GO:0005938 is defined as ''the region of a cell that lies just beneath
      the plasma membrane'', typically an actin-rich cytoplasmic zone. AGTRAP has three transmembrane
      helices and a 52-residue cytoplasmic tail; it is in the membrane, not in the cortical cytoplasm,
      and nothing in the human record (UniProt SUBCELLULAR LOCATION lists ER, Golgi and cytoplasmic
      vesicle membranes only) supports a distinct cortical pool. Marked over-annotated rather than
      removed because the underlying microscopy is real and peripheral staining is compatible with
      the plasma membrane row that is retained.'
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM
      failure_modes:
      - COMPARTMENT_OR_COMPLEX_MISMATCH
      - GRANULARITY_MISMATCH
      source_entities:
      - source_id: UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
        source_label: mouse Agtrap (ATRAP_MOUSE)
        source_status: SUPPORTS_SOURCE_BUT_NOT_TARGET
        comment: Holds GO:0005938 by IDA from PubMed:10358057; the same experiment also supports
          its plasma membrane IDA, which is the term that should transfer.
      residue_claims_not_applicable: A compartment-assignment question, not a residue-level one.
- term:
    id: GO:0008217
    label: regulation of blood pressure
  evidence_type: IBA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000033
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - MGI:MGI:1339977
  - PANTHER:PTN002703102
  review:
    summary: The term is right and the propagation is sound, but its only experimental donor cites
      the wrong paper. Retained as non-core organism-level physiology, rescued by knockout evidence
      that nobody has curated.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: 'Chain traced end to end. The human IBA comes from PANTHER node PTN002703102, one of
      only two IBD annotations in PTHR16521, seeded from MGI:MGI:1339977; mouse Agtrap''s sole experimental
      GO:0008217 row is an IMP citing PubMed:10425188, the Agtr2-knockout paper identified on the
      GO:0004945 row above. So the donor''s citation is defective. The conclusion nonetheless holds
      on independent evidence that GO has not captured: Atrap-deficient mice have significantly
      higher mean systolic blood pressure, higher plasma volume and increased renal-cortical AT1R
      surface expression (PubMed:20093357). Blood-pressure regulation is an organism-level consequence
      of restraining AT1R signalling rather than AGTRAP''s own molecular activity, so it is kept
      as non-core. Recorded as a request to MGI to re-reference the mouse row rather than as a reason
      to drop the human one.'
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:20093357
    - PMID:10425188
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:20093357
      supporting_text: Mean systolic BP was significantly higher in Atrap-/- mice compared with
        wild-type mice.
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: NO_FAILURE_NON_CORE
      failure_modes:
      - SOURCE_MISCITATION
      source_entities:
      - source_id: MGI:MGI:1339977
        source_label: mouse Agtrap
        source_status: SOURCE_BAD
        comment: Its GO:0008217 IMP cites PubMed:10425188, an Agtr2-knockout study. The term is
          nevertheless true of mouse Agtrap on PubMed:20093357, which is uncurated.
      - source_id: PANTHER:PTN002703102
        source_label: PTHR16521 Euteleostomi node
        source_status: SUPPORTS_TRANSFER
        comment: Internal tree node; the family has no paralogues, so the transfer itself is orthologue-to-orthologue.
      residue_claims_not_applicable: An organism-level physiology term; no residue-level claim is
        involved.

  review:
    summary: Correct. UniProt's cytoplasmic vesicle membrane SUBCELLULAR LOCATION line for AGTRAP

- term:
    id: GO:0038166
    label: angiotensin-activated signaling pathway
  evidence_type: IEA
  original_reference_id: GO_REF:0000002
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - InterPro:IPR009436
  review:
    summary: The sign is wrong. This is an InterPro family-name mapping asserting that AGTRAP is
      part of the angiotensin-activated pathway, whereas every measurement on the protein shows
      it damping that pathway.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: 'The row comes from InterPro:IPR009436, the AGTRAP family signature, so the term derives
      from the family''s name rather than from any experiment - the same name-implies-function shape
      as the GO:0004945 row. What has actually been measured runs the other way: ATRAP over-expression
      markedly inhibits AT1a-mediated phospholipase C activation while leaving m3 receptor signalling
      intact (PubMed:10358057), reduces inositol lipid generation, angiotensin-II-stimulated c-fos
      promoter activity and proliferation (PubMed:12960423), and Atrap-null mice show elevated blood
      pressure with increased surface AT1R (PubMed:20093357). GO keeps regulation terms outside
      the process they regulate, so the correct term is GO:0110062 negative regulation of angiotensin-activated
      signaling pathway. Modified rather than removed because the biology the signature was reaching
      for is real; only its direction and role are wrong.'
    proposed_replacement_terms:
    - id: GO:0110062
      label: negative regulation of angiotensin-activated signaling pathway
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:10358057
    - PMID:12960423
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:10358057
      supporting_text: Overexpression of ATRAP in COS-7 cells caused a marked inhibition of AT1a
        receptor-mediated activation of phospholipase C without affecting m3 receptor-mediated activation.
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: a moderate decrease in the generation of inositol lipids, a marked decrease
        in the angiotensin II-stimulated transcriptional activity of the c-fos promoter luciferase
        reporter gene, and a decrease in cell proliferation
    propagation_review:
      root_cause: TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM
      failure_modes:
      - ROLE_CONFLATION
      - REGULATORY_SIGN_INVERSION
      source_entities:
      - source_id: InterPro:IPR009436
        source_label: AGTRAP family signature
        source_status: SUPPORTS_SOURCE_BUT_NOT_TARGET
        comment: A family-name-derived interpro2go mapping; the family is single-subfamily and AGTRAP-specific,
          so the signature is correct - the GO term attached to it is not.
      residue_claims_not_applicable: A pathway-role and direction question, not a residue-level
        one.
- term:
    id: GO:0042802
    label: identical protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:32296183
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q6RW13-2
  isoform: Q6RW13-2
  review:
    summary: A self-interaction recorded only by the CCSB two-hybrid pipeline - on isoform 2 in
      HuRI, and on the canonical protein in two earlier releases - with no orthogonal test of AGTRAP
      oligomerisation anywhere.
    action: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED
    reason: 'The GOA row rests on PMID:32296183, where Q6RW13-2 was paired with itself, and IntAct
      logs that one screen under three sub-method names, so its apparent replicate count is an artefact
      of the sub-method vocabulary rather than of independent assays. IntAct does record the self-pair
      more than once - PMID:16189514 and PMID:25416956 also report a canonical Q6RW13 self-pair
      - but all three are the same CCSB clone collection in the same two-hybrid system, so they
      are recurrence on one platform rather than replication across methods. Homodimerisation of
      a three-pass membrane protein is plausible a priori but has never been tested by crosslinking,
      co-immunoprecipitation of differentially tagged copies, or any size-based method, and the
      tested species is isoform 2, which lacks residues 115-121 from within the AGTR1-interaction
      region 110-122. Marked over-annotated rather than removed: the observation stands, its weight
      does not.'
- term:
    id: GO:0031702
    label: type 1 angiotensin receptor binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:12960423
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P30556
  review:
    summary: Proposed. This is the interaction the gene is named for, it is measured, UniProt curates
      it on the human entry and gives it a sequence feature, and the mouse orthologue carries it
      in GO - yet human GOA has no trace of it.
    action: NEW
    reason: 'AGTRAP was isolated as a binder of the AT1a receptor''s carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic
      domain, and the binding is subtype-selective: PubMed:10358057 tested AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin
      B2, endothelin B and beta2-adrenergic tails and found none of them bound. PubMed:12960423
      mapped the requirement to AGTRAP''s own C-terminal tail by deletion, and UniProt records the
      interaction on the human entry (SUBUNIT with ECO:0000269) plus a REGION 110..122 feature annotated
      ''Interaction with AGTR1''. The mouse orthologue already carries this as GO:0005515 IPI with
      P29754 (Agtr1a) from PubMed:10358057; the human gene carries 187 protein binding rows, none
      of them AGTR1. GO:0031702 is chosen over its parent GO:0031701 because the measured fact is
      precisely the subtype selectivity. The term is already established for proteins that bind
      the receptor''s cytoplasmic face rather than its ligand pocket, so this is not a novel use
      of it: of its 197 annotations over 188 gene products, 16 entities hold it by non-IEA evidence,
      and those include ARRB2, JAK2, TYK2 and ARAP1, each by rat IPI, alongside AGT (the ligand
      precursor; human IPI, mouse IDA). What is thin is human coverage - five human entities, of
      which only AGT and BDKRB2 are IPI and the other three are Ensembl projections - and none of
      them is an accessory protein of AGTRAP''s kind. Evidence code, stated with its difficulty
      rather than asserted. IPI on PubMed:12960423 rests on two things. First, UniProt tags that
      paper with ECO:0000269 on the human entry for FUNCTION, SUBUNIT and SUBCELLULAR LOCATION -
      a curator judgement made with the full text, which this review does not have (PMC284805 returns
      no extractable body). Second, NLM indexes PubMed:12960423 with the MeSH organism term ''Humans''
      and with neither ''Animals'' nor ''Mice'', whereas the founding mouse paper PubMed:10358057
      is indexed ''Animals'' + ''Mice'' and not ''Humans''. The indexing discriminates the two papers,
      and the absence of ''Animals'' is hard to account for if the experiments had used mouse material.
      Against that sits a real discrepancy that should not be buried: the abstract numbers the protein''s
      hydrophobic domains 14-36, 55-77 and 88-108 with a cytoplasmic tail at 109-161, and 161 aa
      is mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0), not human Q6RW13 (159 aa, TOPO_DOM 108..159). The likeliest reconciliation
      is that the authors kept the residue numbering of the sequence first published in PubMed:10358057
      while working with human constructs, but that cannot be confirmed without the full text. IPI
      is therefore retained on explicit deference to the UniProt curator, with the numbering conflict
      recorded; if the full text shows rodent constructs, the correct code is ISS with UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
      and the supporting entity becomes the murine AT1a receptor UniProtKB:P29754 rather than human
      AGTR1 UniProtKB:P30556 - the code and the partner accession change together, and the term
      does not change either way. The founding characterisation (PubMed:10358057) used the mouse
      protein and mouse AT1a and is cited as corroboration rather than as the human evidence.'
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:10358057
    - PMID:11733189
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: Mutant forms of ATRAP lacking the carboxyl end are unable to bind to the
        AT1 receptor, leading to the formation of prominent perinuclear vesicle clusters.
    - reference_id: PMID:10358057
      supporting_text: ATRAP interacts specifically with the carboxyl-terminal domain of the AT1a
        receptor but not with those of angiotensin II type 2 (AT2), m3 muscarinic acetylcholine,
        bradykinin B2, endothelin B, and beta2-adrenergic receptors.
    - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: 'CC   -!- SUBUNIT: Interacts with RACK1, and with the C-terminal region of
        AGTR1.'
    - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: FT                   /note="Interaction with AGTR1"
- term:
    id: GO:0002092
    label: positive regulation of receptor internalization
  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: PMID:11162453
  qualifier: involved_in
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
  review:
    summary: Proposed. Promoting AT1 receptor internalization is the mechanism UniProt names in
      AGTRAP's FUNCTION line and the one every downstream phenotype is explained by, and GO records
      nothing like it.
    action: NEW
    reason: 'Over-expression of ATRAP potentiates angiotensin-II-stimulated AT1 receptor internalization
      in vascular smooth muscle cells (PubMed:11162453) and lowers AT1 receptor number at the cardiomyocyte
      surface (PubMed:15757644), and the corresponding loss-of-function result is that Atrap-null
      mice show enhanced surface AT1 receptor in the renal cortex (PubMed:20093357). UniProt''s
      human FUNCTION line states the mechanism directly - a negative regulator acting ''by regulating
      receptor internalization''. The evidence code is ISS rather than IMP on the same test applied
      to the GO:0031702 row, and here it comes out the other way: NLM indexes PubMed:11162453 with
      ''Animals'' and ''Rats'' and no ''Humans'' term, and PubMed:15757644 with ''Animals'' and
      ''Mice'' and no ''Humans''. Both are rodent over-expression experiments, so the claim for
      the human protein is made by orthology to mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0) and is deliberately not asserted
      as a direct human observation. Proposed in addition to, not instead of, the GO:0110062 replacement
      on the InterPro row: that term states the outcome, this one states how it is achieved.'
    additional_reference_ids:
    - PMID:15757644
    - PMID:20093357
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:11162453
      supporting_text: Transfection of ATRAP potentiated AT1 receptor internalization upon Ang II
        stimulation in these VSMCs.
    - reference_id: PMID:20093357
      supporting_text: (125)I-AngII binding showed enhanced surface expression of AT1 receptors
        in the renal cortex of Atrap-/- mice, accompanied by increased carboanhydrase-sensitive
        proximal tubular function.
    - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: 'CC   -!- FUNCTION: Appears to be a negative regulator of type-1 angiotensin
        II'
- term:
    id: GO:0141109
    label: transporter activator activity
  evidence_type: ISS
  original_reference_id: PMID:27015675
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:Q9WVK0
  review:
    summary: 'Proposed. A second, AT1-receptor-independent molecular activity: AGTRAP binds the
      cardiac calcium pump SERCA2a and increases its calcium uptake. Absent from GO in every form.'
    action: NEW
    reason: 'PubMed:27015675 is titled for SERCA2a rather than for AGTRAP, which is why an AGTRAP-keyed
      search does not surface it. It identifies SERCA2a in Atrap pull-downs by MALDI-MS, confirms
      the interaction by co-immunoprecipitation and by surface plasmon resonance, and shows Atrap
      increases SERCA-dependent calcium uptake in isolated sarcoplasmic reticulum vesicles; Atrap-null
      myocytes have prolonged calcium-transient decay and sarcomere re-lengthening, and the mice
      a markedly reduced maximum ventricular filling rate with unchanged ejection fraction. GO:0141109
      ''binds to and increases the activity of a transporter'' is the sibling of GO:0141110, which
      phospholamban holds by IDA for the inhibitory version of the same regulation, so the ontology
      already models this relationship. The knockout physiology is unambiguously mouse, hence ISS
      with mouse Agtrap as the supporting entity rather than IDA. One caveat in the other direction,
      recorded so it can be revisited: NLM indexes PubMed:27015675 with ''Humans'' as well as ''Animals'',
      and with ''HEK293 Cells'', so the binding measurements may have used human constructs even
      though the calcium-uptake and knockout work did not. ISS is the conservative reading; confirming
      human constructs would license IPI for the interaction half. Stated as one well-controlled
      study, not as settled biology.'
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:27015675
      supporting_text: Sequencing by MALDI-MS of the isolated complexes showed that Atrap interacts
        with the cardiac Ca(2+)-ATPase SERCA2a.
    - reference_id: PMID:27015675
      supporting_text: Atrap enhanced the SERCA-dependent Ca(2+) uptake in isolated SR membrane
        vesicles.

- id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-deep-research-affinage.md
  title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGTRAP (human)
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: 'Machine-generated provider record; gates_passed True, faith 100%, 21 citations,
      all real numeric PMIDs with no preprint identifiers, and none of them retracted or under erratum.
      Its recall was better than this campaign''s average: it supplied the three partner-titled
      papers that carry the review''s positive findings (PubMed:21728994, PubMed:27015675, PubMed:35414770).
      It missed PubMed:35671117, the only orthogonal validation of a two-hybrid partner, and both
      donor references (PubMed:10425188, PubMed:17033689) that produced the review''s largest defects
      - those came from querying donor evidence, not from literature search. Quoted here only for
      its corpus-level partner list, never for a mechanistic claim.'
core_functions:
- description: Selective binding partner and negative regulator of the type-1 angiotensin II receptor.
    AGTRAP's cytoplasmic C-terminal tail, and specifically the region around residues 110-122, engages
    the AT1 receptor's own carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic tail; the interaction does not extend to
    AT2, m3 muscarinic, bradykinin B2, endothelin B or beta2-adrenergic receptors. AGTRAP cycles
    on endoplasmic-reticulum-, Golgi- and endosome-derived vesicles that translocate constitutively
    toward the plasma membrane, and the effect of the interaction is to accelerate AT1 receptor
    internalization and lower its surface density, so that angiotensin II produces less phospholipase
    C activation, less inositol lipid generation, less c-fos induction and less proliferation. Losing
    the protein in mouse raises surface AT1 receptor in the renal cortex and raises arterial blood
    pressure.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0031702
    label: type 1 angiotensin receptor binding
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0110062
    label: negative regulation of angiotensin-activated signaling pathway
  - id: GO:0002092
    label: positive regulation of receptor internalization
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005789
    label: endoplasmic reticulum membrane
  - id: GO:0000139
    label: Golgi membrane
  - id: GO:0030659
    label: cytoplasmic vesicle membrane
  - id: GO:0005886
    label: plasma membrane
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:10358057
    supporting_text: ATRAP interacts specifically with the carboxyl-terminal domain of the AT1a
      receptor but not with those of angiotensin II type 2 (AT2), m3 muscarinic acetylcholine, bradykinin
      B2, endothelin B, and beta2-adrenergic receptors.
  - reference_id: PMID:12960423
    supporting_text: Mutant forms of ATRAP lacking the carboxyl end are unable to bind to the AT1
      receptor, leading to the formation of prominent perinuclear vesicle clusters.
  - reference_id: PMID:11162453
    supporting_text: Transfection of ATRAP potentiated AT1 receptor internalization upon Ang II
      stimulation in these VSMCs.
  - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-uniprot.txt
    supporting_text: FT                   /note="Interaction with AGTR1"
  - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-deep-research-affinage.md
    supporting_text: '- **partners:** AGTR1, RACK1, PITPNC1, ATP2A2, USP14, PBX3, PSMB8, PSMB10'
  knowledge_gaps:
  - gap_statement: The AGTRAP-AGTR1 interface is unmapped. No structure of the complex exists, and
      UniProt's REGION 110..122 'Interaction with AGTR1' feature carries no evidence code at all,
      so no individual contact residue on either partner has been identified.
    boundary: 'Firmly established: the interaction is subtype-selective for AT1 over five other
      receptor tails, it requires AGTRAP''s cytoplasmic carboxy-terminal region (deleting it abolishes
      binding), and it engages the receptor''s own carboxy-terminal cytoplasmic domain.'
    gap_kind:
    - BIOLOGY
    dark_aspect: RESIDUAL_SUBGAP
    significance: Without mapped contacts there is no way to build a separation-of-function allele,
      so every cellular result rests on over-expression or whole-gene deletion and cannot distinguish
      the receptor-binding activity from AGTRAP's other activities.
    resolution: Alanine scanning across AGTRAP residues 108-140 coupled to a surface-AT1R internalization
      readout, or a structure of the complex.
    provenance:
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: Mutant forms of ATRAP lacking the carboxyl end are unable to bind to the
        AT1 receptor, leading to the formation of prominent perinuclear vesicle clusters.
    - reference_id: file:human/AGTRAP/AGTRAP-uniprot.txt
      supporting_text: FT   REGION          110..122
  - gap_statement: 'Where AGTRAP acts on the receptor is unknown: whether it intercepts AT1R during
      biosynthetic delivery, accelerates retrieval from the plasma membrane, or both.'
    boundary: 'Firmly established: AGTRAP''s steady-state pool is intracellular - endoplasmic reticulum,
      Golgi and endocytic vesicles - while its vesicles translocate constitutively toward the plasma
      membrane, and its measured effect is a reduction in surface AT1 receptor number.'
    gap_kind:
    - BIOLOGY
    dark_aspect: RESIDUAL_SUBGAP
    significance: The two mechanisms predict opposite therapeutic strategies for raising AGTRAP
      activity, and they are the difference between an ER retention factor and an endocytic adaptor.
    resolution: Pulse-chase surface biotinylation of AT1R in AGTRAP-knockout versus wild-type cells,
      separating newly delivered from resident receptor.
    provenance:
    - reference_id: PMID:12960423
      supporting_text: Real-time tracking of ATRAP vesicles shows constitutive translocation toward
        the plasma membrane.
- description: Stimulator of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2a in cardiac muscle,
    independent of any angiotensin receptor. AGTRAP binds SERCA2a directly and raises its calcium
    uptake rate, speeding cytosolic calcium decay and sarcomere re-lengthening; losing the protein
    slows ventricular filling without changing contractile amplitude or ejection fraction. This
    is the mirror image of phospholamban, which binds the same pump and inhibits it. Recorded because
    it is a directly measured activity rather than an inference from the gene's name, but it rests
    on a single study carried out entirely in mouse.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0141109
    label: transporter activator activity
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:27015675
    supporting_text: Atrap enhanced the SERCA-dependent Ca(2+) uptake in isolated SR membrane vesicles.
  - reference_id: PMID:27015675
    supporting_text: The interaction between Atrap and SERCA2a was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation
      and by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy.
  knowledge_gaps:
  - gap_statement: Whether the human protein stimulates SERCA2a at all is untested, and in no species
      is the binding site, the stoichiometry, or the relationship to phospholamban known - so it
      is unknown whether AGTRAP is an independent activator or a competitor that displaces an inhibitor
      from the same groove.
    boundary: 'Firmly established in mouse: Atrap and SERCA2a associate by pull-down, co-immunoprecipitation
      and surface plasmon resonance, Atrap increases SERCA-dependent calcium uptake in isolated
      sarcoplasmic reticulum vesicles, and Atrap-null myocytes and hearts show slowed relaxation
      and filling with normal contractile amplitude.'
    gap_kind:
    - BIOLOGY
    dark_aspect: RESIDUAL_SUBGAP
    significance: Activators of SERCA2a are a small and therapeutically interesting class; whether
      AGTRAP joins it, and whether it works by competing with phospholamban, determines how the
      two regulatory inputs combine in failing myocardium.
    resolution: Reconstituted calcium-uptake and surface plasmon resonance assays with human AGTRAP
      and human ATP2A2, including a phospholamban competition arm, plus a crosslinking or structural
      map of the contact.
    provenance:
    - reference_id: PMID:27015675
      supporting_text: The angiotensin II type 1 receptor-associated protein (Atrap) is highly expressed
        in the heart, but its function in the heart is unknown.
suggested_questions:
- question: 'MGI annotation request: mouse Agtrap (MGI:1339977) carries GO:0004945 angiotensin type
    II receptor activity (enables, IMP) and GO:0008217 (IMP) from PMID:10425188, which is an Agtr2-knockout
    study that assays no Agtrap allele; Agtr2 correctly receives GO:0004945 from the same paper.
    Retiring the GO:0004945 row would also clear the Ensembl projections onto human AGTRAP and rat
    Agtrap and the ISO copy RGD makes from it - one edit fixing four annotations in three species.
    The GO:0008217 row should be re-referenced to PMID:20093357 rather than retired, since the Atrap-knockout
    blood pressure phenotype is real.'
  experts:
  - Dzau VJ
  - Tamura K
  - Horiuchi M
- question: 'Why does human AGTRAP have 187 protein binding rows and not one of them AGTR1, when
    UniProt curates the interaction on the human entry with ECO:0000269, gives it a REGION 110..122
    feature, and the mouse orthologue holds it as GO:0005515 IPI with P29754? The same applies to
    RACK1 (P63244), supported by four orthogonal assays in PMID:11733189. Checking from the partners''
    side rather than AGTRAP''s shows the gap is symmetric, so it is not a property of this gene''s
    record: PMID:12960423, PMID:11733189, PMID:21728994, PMID:27015675 and PMID:35414770 have produced
    zero GO annotations on human AGTR1, RACK1, PITPNC1, ATP2A2 and canonical PBX3 respectively.
    The one counter-example shows it is fixable - MGI curated PMID:35671117 reciprocally on both
    mouse partners (Fam114a1 IPI with Q9WVK0, Agtrap IPI with Q9D281), while neither human partner
    received anything.'
  experts:
  - Cockcroft S
  - Orchard S
- question: 'GO:0031702 type 1 angiotensin receptor binding carries 197 annotations over 188 gene
    products, but only 16 entities hold it by non-IEA evidence and the experimental weight sits
    almost entirely in rat: ARRB2, JAK2, TYK2 and ARAP1 each by IPI. Only five human entities hold
    the term at all, and only AGT and BDKRB2 by IPI. Should those rat IPIs be projected to their
    human orthologues, and is the AT1 receptor''s cytoplasmic interactome being under-annotated
    in human as a result?'
  experts: []
- question: GOA imported all 188 of AGTRAP's binding rows from two-hybrid screens and none from
    the 23 IntAct pairs with AP-MS, co-IP or BioID support, which are almost all membrane proteins
    (CYB5D2, ENPP6, MBLAC2, TMEM47, TMEM106B, LAMP5, SLC15A3, SLC15A4, TMEM63A, CFTR, PAFAH2). Is
    that selection deliberate, and would the membrane set be a better basis for annotating a three-pass
    membrane protein?
  experts:
  - Orchard S
  - Vidal M
- question: Does human AGTRAP stimulate SERCA2a as the mouse protein does (PMID:27015675), and is
    the activity confined to SERCA2a or shared with SERCA1 and SERCA3? If it generalises, GO:1901896
    positive regulation of ATPase-coupled calcium transmembrane transporter activity would belong
    on the gene alongside the molecular function proposed here.
  experts:

- question: Is the AGTRAP homodimer real? The only evidence is a single HuRI self-pair on isoform
    2, which lacks residues 115-121 from within the AGTR1-interaction region - so if the protein
    does oligomerise, the tested species is the one least likely to be engaging the receptor.
  experts:

- question: 'Both ISS rows proposed here (GO:0002092, GO:0141109) transfer from mouse Agtrap (Q9WVK0),
    which holds neither term - so as written they are ISS from an ortholog with nothing to transfer.
    The underlying experiments are mouse, so the annotations belong on the mouse gene first: Agtrap

  experts:
  - Castrop H
  - Kockskamper J
- question: GO:0043495 protein-membrane adaptor activity is defined as bringing a protein to a membrane
    'either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein', yet SUN1, SUN2
    and GPR179 all hold it and are themselves integral membrane proteins that satisfy neither clause
    - as would AGTRAP, which anchors PITPNC1 by being the membrane protein. Should the differentia
    be widened to cover an integral membrane protein acting as the tether, rather than leaving each
    such annotation to be justified per gene?

suggested_experiments:
- hypothesis: AGTRAP and AGTR1 associate at endogenous expression in the tissues where both are
    abundant, and the interaction's absence from human GOA is a curation gap rather than a biological
    one.
  description: Co-immunoprecipitate endogenous AGTRAP and AGTR1 from human kidney proximal tubule
    or cardiac tissue at native expression, and submit the result to IntAct. Every existing AGTRAP-AGTR1
    experiment is an over-expression assay, several of them on the mouse protein, which is the likeliest
    reason the interaction never entered human GOA.
  experiment_type: Endogenous co-immunoprecipitation from human tissue
- hypothesis: The AGTR1-binding determinant lies within AGTRAP residues 108-140, and isoform 2,
    which deletes residues 115-121 from that region, is impaired for receptor regulation.
  description: Map the AGTRAP side of the interface by scanning alanine substitutions across residues
    108-140 in a surface-AT1R internalization assay, then test whether the isoform-2 deletion (residues
    115-121) is loss-of-function. That would say whether the two main isoforms differ in receptor
    regulation and would replace UniProt's unevidenced REGION 110..122 with mapped contacts.
  experiment_type: Alanine-scanning mutagenesis with a receptor internalization readout
- hypothesis: Human AGTRAP stimulates human SERCA2a as the mouse proteins do, and does so by competing
    with phospholamban for an overlapping site.
  description: Repeat the SERCA2a calcium-uptake and surface plasmon resonance experiments of PMID:27015675
    with human AGTRAP and human ATP2A2, including a phospholamban competition arm, to establish
    whether the activity is conserved and whether the two regulators share a site.
  experiment_type: Reconstituted calcium-uptake assay and surface plasmon resonance
- hypothesis: The large majority of AGTRAP's two-hybrid partners do not reproduce in a membrane-compatible
    assay, and the reproduction rate is far lower for partners confined to compartments its cytosolic
    tail cannot reach.
  description: Retest a stratified sample of the two-hybrid partners in a membrane-compatible assay
    - split-ubiquitin, NanoBiT, or proximity labelling from AGTRAP in cells - sampling separately
    from the topologically accessible partners and from the 28 confined to the mitochondrial matrix,
    the nucleoplasm or the extracellular space. The second group is a built-in negative control,
    and the resulting hit rate would calibrate how much of this gene's binding record to believe.
  experiment_type: Membrane-compatible interaction assay (split-ubiquitin / NanoBiT / proximity
    labelling)
- hypothesis: AGTRAP lowers surface AT1 receptor by accelerating retrieval from the plasma membrane
    rather than by retaining newly synthesised receptor intracellularly.
  description: Determine whether AGTRAP acts on newly synthesised or on surface AT1 receptor by
    pulse-chase surface biotinylation in AGTRAP-knockout versus wild-type cells. Its steady-state
    pool is intracellular while its measured effect is on surface receptor number, and no published
    experiment distinguishes retention during delivery from accelerated retrieval.
  experiment_type: Pulse-chase cell-surface biotinylation in a knockout background
